Definition: from a compound of G2095 and G4383; to be of good countenance, i.e. (figuratively) to make a display:--make a fair show.
BiblicalUsage: In the New Testament, euprosōpéō is the word for make a fair show. In Galatians 6:12, the text says "As many as desire to make a fair shew in the flesh."
TheologicalSignificance: For me, euprosōpéō means make a fair show, nothing more and nothing less.
